seat.BEST_WHY: The floor in the lit region (roughly x 200–720, y 460–720) is built from stones of unequal size — a large slab under the figure's feet at (330–400, 520–570) sits next to half-width stones to its right — and the joints are single dark lines that thicken and thin along one run rather than a uniform grid. Two long cracks (one from (200,470) sweeping down through (330,590) to (400,720); the arc at (560–750, 640–720)) cross several stones without breaking at joints, so the floor reads as one cracked surface, not tiles. The wall cap along y 395–450 is a timber beam with driven pins at (290,430), (400,430), (490,430), (580,430), (660,430), (740,430), and the pins are not evenly spaced — that is the orcs' repair, drawn straight, no joke in it. The crossed timbers at (440,615) are lashed with rope at the crossing, again matching the fiction. Light falloff is smooth with no visible band edges, and the corridor at (505–540, 60–430) is lit from the bottom up as it should be.
seat.WORST_WHY: The grey wall is a single stamped block repeated — the bottom band (0–384, 190–288) is six rows of the identical brick, the left column (0–48, 0–190) the same brick again, with the same dark outline on every one; the repetition is visible at a glance. There is no top-surface/face distinction anywhere, so the grey reads as a second floor material rather than a wall, and the room has no enclosure. The dirt floor (50–248, 0–190) is uniform speckle noise with a few random blue specks at (150,180) and (200,60) that belong to nothing. The pool (248–345, 0–190) is a flat green rectangle with a 1px hard edge against both dirt and stone — no bank, no depth, and the pale blobs in it at (320,25), (330,120), (265,160) are soft-edged in a hard-pixel image. The scatter of white pixels at (210–235, 110–130) reads as a glitch. And there is no light falloff at all: the figure at (222,10) carries no light, the whole map is one flat value.

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
item_exit.item: #212 round 2 — the Λ-frame against the north wall: 'feet land on the cap band, not below it; no reveal foot visible under it. Also brighter and more saturated than the X-frame under the same fire' (Rafe, props walk, 2026-09-13)
item_exit.claim: a prop placed against a wall stands on the floor at the reveal's foot, in front of the face, and is never overdrawn by the cap; the barricade family is one wood, and every lit difference between its members is the rig's.
item_exit.measured: MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/jamb/, m_flat + jamb_m_shadow). (a) The sprite's bottom wood row sat at frame y 544 against a reveal foot at 546/547 — the SPRITE was at the foot, as the report said; the EYE was right too, because §3.2's base parallelogram rises ½·0.35·cell = 11 px up-right from that row (ReviewLighting's occluder draws exactly it), so the whole footprint lay over the FACE: feet inside the wall. (b) The cap's upper half was re-laid over the prop (cap_bands_over_props=2) — the law says never. (c) Flat-lit wood albedo: Λ (84,62,42) vs X (91,66,44), same hue ratios (r/g 1.36/1.38, g/b 1.45/1.49) — one wood. At the regime Λ reads L 73 r/g 1.74 against X's 47/1.63 because Λ is 1.4 tiles from the fire (reach 4.0) and X 6.3 — not the same fire. FIX: shift = cell − margin − PropBaseRun (one constant, shared with the occluder), so the base's far edge meets the foot and its near edge sits 11 px onto the floor; the cap-band re-lay removed. MEASURED AFTER (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/lambda/): flat-lit, the sprite's bottom wood row moved from 544 to 556 — 12 px, the 11.2-px run rounded to the pixel grid — so the base's far edge sits on the foot and its near edge 11 px onto the floor cell; the wall's foot line shows between the legs. No Tier1CapBand node exists (the counter is gone from the boundary line); the apex draws over the cap's near half and stops 12 px short of the cap's top. east_faces=5(ground-mask) unchanged. Albedo unchanged (no pixel of either sprite moved). JUDGE (Rafe, 2026-09-13): the fine fact — bottom row at foot + 12, zero cap pixels over the lower half — is the DERIVED ASSERTION this exit carries; the deck's grounding plant is the coarse failure (lambda-in-the-face).
item_exit.instrument: wood-pixel rows and flat-lit albedo (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/jamb/face_stats.py family), the [Tier1] boundary summary line; builder's measurements, none a gate
